city.pop_note: 1000-1787: estimates in the Spanish Wikipedia demography annex (S46; the 1000 and 1480 figures are credited there to Trapiello 2020, not re-checked); 1560 matches 'unlikely more than 20,000' in S1. The 860 point repeats the c.1000 figure as a PLACEHOLDER [Guessing]: no source for the 9th century. The annex also lists 60,000 for 1565 and 180,000 for 1790, left out as odd jumps. 1842-2021: INE census (de jure) figures as shown in S46 (the 1825 estimate of 201,000 is left out: it would show a drop to the 1842 census). 2024: municipal register figure in S46 (labelled 'census' for the HUD); S49 says over 3.4 million in 2025. The municipal area grew by annexations 1948-1954 (S1), so the series is not like-for-like.

polities.name: Emirate of Córdoba · Mayrit
polities.note: Emirate 756-929 (S4); Mayrit founded under Muhammad I (S3).

polities.name: Taifa of Toledo
polities.note: Taifa emerged after 1018 (S5); Madrid lies in its greatest extent (S5). 1035 (S5 'around 1035', Dhunnunid takeover of Toledo) is a modelling choice; the caliphate fell in 1031 (S4).

polities.name: Crown of Castile · Alfonso VI
polities.note: Conquest 1083/1085 (S1); Alfonso VI ruled León and Castile from 1072 (S6). The name 'Crown of Castile' is the later label.

polities.name: Catholic Monarchs · Castile and Aragon
polities.note: Dynastic union of Castile and Aragon in 1479 (S6).

polities.name: Napoleonic Spain · Joseph Bonaparte
polities.note: Napoleon hands the throne to Joseph on 5 May 1808 (S1).

polities.name: Bourbon Restoration · Ferdinand VII
polities.note: Ferdinand VII returns to the throne in 1814 (S1).

polities.name: Glorious Revolution · First Republic
polities.note: Sept 1868 revolution (S1); the First Republic was ended on 29 December 1874 (S41). Years 1868-1874 are grouped: the republic's start year is not in the fetched text.

polities.name: Democratic Spain

S1.title: Wikipedia EN, History of Madrid
S1.quote: By the late 10th century, Majriṭ was an important borderland military stronghold … Although he made no official declaration, the seat of the court became the de facto capital … The population plummeted (reportedly reduced to a half) during the 5-year period … led to the confiscation of ecclesiastical properties and the subsequent demolition of churches, convents … meant the introduction of the first collective system of transportation in the city … Conquered by Christians in 1083 or 1085 … The primitive urban nucleus of Madrid (Majriṭ) was founded in the late 9th century (from 852 to 886) as a citadel erected on behalf of Muhammad I … Extending across roughly 8 ha … historiography debates whether if the event took place in 1083 … The town briefly hosted a medieval mint, manufacturing coins from 1467 to 1471 … the comunero rebels deposed the corregidor, named Antonio de Astudillo, by 17 June 1520 … Philip II (1527–1598), moved the court to Madrid in 1561 … approaching the 100,000 mark by the end of the 16th century … the 5-year period the capital was set in Valladolid (1601–1606) … massive riots erupted in March 1766 in Madrid … On 2 May 1808 (Spanish: Dos de Mayo), the Madrileños revolted against the French forces … On 12 August 1812, following the defeat of the French forces at Salamanca, English and Portuguese troops entered Madrid … The reforms enacted by Finance Minister Juan Álvarez Mendizábal in 1835–1836 led to the confiscation of ecclesiastical properties … The Canal de Isabel II was inaugurated on 24 June 1858 … The plan for the Ensanche de Madrid ('widening of Madrid') by Carlos María de Castro was passed through a royal decree issued on 19 July 1860 … The creation of the Salamanca–Sol–Pozas tram service in Madrid in 1871 … the works formally started in April 1910 with a ceremony led by King Alfonso XIII … In 1919 the Madrid Metro (known as the Ferrocarril Metropolitano by that time) inaugurated its first service, which went from Sol to the Cuatro Caminos area. … After the proclamation of the Second Republic on 14 April 1931 … On 20 July armed workers and loyal troops stormed the single focus of resistance, the Cuartel de La Montaña … Madrid, besieged from October 1936, saw a major offensive in its western suburbs in November of that year. … The city fell to the nationalists on 28 March 1939. … Madrid proper was bombed for the first time in the night of 27–28 August 1936 … the municipality greatly increased in size through the annexation of 13 surrounding municipalities … The population of the city peaked in 1975 … killing 191 people and injuring 1,800 … Glorious Revolution resulting in the deposition of Queen Isabella II started with a pronunciamiento in the bay of Cádiz in September 1868 … Napoleon forced both kings to abdicate on 5 May, handing the throne to his brother Joseph Bonaparte … After the war of independence Ferdinand VII returned to the throne (1814)

S2.title: Wikipedia EN, Walls of Madrid
S2.quote: Umayyad Emir of Cordoba Muhammad I ordered the walls to be built between the years 860 and 880 … The Christian Walls of Madrid, also known as the Medieval Walls, were built between the 11th and 12th centuries … they were most likely constructed around 1438 … The Walls of Philip II were constructed by Philip II, in 1566, for fiscal and sanitary control … The Walls of Felipe IV were built around the city of Madrid between 1625 and 1868 … Ruins of the walls still stand along the Calle Mayor street, at number 83 … A long section exists under the Plaza de la Armería … The first of these, known from 1126, was the Arrabal of Saint Martin … the population increasing from 5,000 to 12,000 inhabitants from the mid-15th to early 16th century … the walls fell into disuse and were almost entirely demolished

S3.title: Wikipedia EN, Royal Alcázar of Madrid
S3.quote: This original fortress was erected by the Umayyad amir Muhammad I of Córdoba (852–886) between 860 and 880 … originally built in the second half of the ninth century by the Muslims

S4.title: Wikipedia EN, Umayyad state of Córdoba
S4.quote: The Emirate of Córdoba, and from 929, the Caliphate of Córdoba, was an Arab Islamic state ruled by the Umayyad dynasty from 756 to 1031 … From 756 it was ruled as an independent emirate until Abd al-Rahman III proclaimed himself as caliph in 929 … In 1031, after years of infighting, the caliphate collapsed and fractured into a number of independent Muslim taifa

S5.title: Wikipedia EN, Taifa of Toledo
S5.quote: It emerged after 1018 upon the fracturing of the Caliphate of Córdoba … It lasted until the Christian conquest of Toledo in 1085 … and Madrid (to the Sierra de Guadarrama)

zones.name: Mayrit: Muslim citadel and town
zones.note: [Certain] the citadel was raised between 860 and 880 (S3, S8) and covered about 4 ha / 980 m of wall (S8); S1 says roughly 8 ha counting the alcazar and the wider citadel. [Guessing] the ring is a HAND SKETCH (+-100 m) around the Alcazar/Almudena ridge scaled to 4 ha; houses of 4-7 m are a modelling choice.

zones.name: Christian walled town
zones.note: [Certain] wall of a bit over 33 ha and about 2,200 m (S7), begun after 1083/1085 and still unfinished in 1202 (S7). [Guessing] ring is a HAND SKETCH scaled to 33 ha; the 1085-1202 ramp from the Alcazar is a modelling choice, not a measured growth.

zones.name: Medieval suburbs (arrabales) and the 15th-century wall
zones.note: [Certain] the Arrabal of San Martin is known from 1126, the suburb wall is most likely c. 1438 and its southern part was extended around 1520, population 5,000 to 12,000 from the mid-15th to the early 16th century (S2). [Guessing] ring is a HAND SKETCH following the streets listed in S2; the 1126-1520 ramp from Puerta del Sol is a modelling choice.

zones.name: Habsburg Madrid inside Philip IV's wall (western part)
zones.note: [Certain] the court settles in 1561 and the city nears 100,000 by 1600 (S1); the wall of 1625 encloses 500 ha (S9). [Guessing] ring is a HAND SKETCH of the built-up west and south of the wall (the Retiro and the east are left to the default growth front); the 1561-1700 ramp from Sol is a modelling choice.

zones.name: Ensanche (Castro plan)
zones.note: [Certain] plan approved in 1860 and carried out from 1871 (S10). [Guessing] ring is a HAND SKETCH of the ring around the 1868-demolished wall, NOT the plan's legal boundary; born 1871-1900 and 14-20 m heights are modelling choices. Cost to be measured by QA before any GO.

walls.name: Muslim wall of Mayrit
walls.note: [Certain] ordered between 860 and 880, about 980 m long, 12 feet (about 3.5 m) thick (S2, S8); remains at Calle Mayor 83 and under the Plaza de la Armeria (S2, kept as circles, positions sketched). [Guessing] height 9 m; demolition 1561-1620 is a modelling choice (S2 only says the Christian walls fell into disuse after 1561).

walls.name: Christian wall of Madrid
walls.note: [Certain] built after the conquest, unfinished in 1202, ~2,200 m (S7); fell into disuse and was almost entirely demolished after 1561 (S2). [Guessing] 1090 start, the 1561-1620 demolition window, height 8 m, tower spacing and ring shape (HAND SKETCH).

walls.name: Philip IV's wall (Cerca)
walls.note: [Certain] ordered in 1625, brick, mortar and earth, ~13 km, 500 ha, already covering the Retiro, Atocha and Principe Pio by 1650, torn down in 1868 (S9); the Puerta de Alcala stands in the city wall (S36, kept). [Guessing] ring is a HAND SKETCH following the streets listed in S2; 1650 end of construction and 4 m height are modelling choices.

gutting.name: Gran Vía, section 1 (Alcalá to Red de San Luis)
gutting.note: [Certain] first section built 1910-1917 (S21; S22 says 1910-1915 plus official completion in 1917). [Guessing] strip 42 m wide along a hand-drawn centreline.

gutting.name: Gran Vía, section 2 (Red de San Luis to Callao)
gutting.note: [Certain] second section 1917-1921 (S21) or 1917-1922 (S22); the later year is used. [Guessing] strip 42 m wide, hand-drawn centreline.

gutting.name: Gran Vía, section 3 (Callao to Plaza de España)
gutting.note: [Certain] third section started 1925 and the street was completed in 1929 (S21). [Guessing] strip 42 m wide, hand-drawn centreline.

lost.name: Teatro de los Caños del Peral
lost.note: [Certain] theatre opened 1738 and demolished in 1817 to clear the site of the Teatro Real (S37). [Guessing] block 75 x 55 m, height 14 m.

fires.name: Plaza Mayor fire of 1631
fires.note: [Certain] the first of several fires was in 1631 (S13). [Guessing] month and duration unknown; ring is a 140 x 105 m box on the plaza; no building is destroyed.

fires.name: Plaza Mayor fire of 1790
fires.note: [Certain] nearly a third of the square was destroyed in 1790 (S13). [Guessing] month and duration unknown; no building is destroyed in the model.

fires.name: Alcázar fire
fires.note: [Certain] Christmas Eve 1734, the fire lasted four days and destroyed the old alcazar (S11). [Guessing] ring is a 170 x 130 m box; the alcazar is removed by its landmark demolition, not by the fire.

fires.name: Siege of Madrid western front
fires.note: [Certain] Madrid besieged from October 1936 and a major offensive in the western suburbs in November (S1, S34). [Guessing] the ring is a 900 x 700 m sketch near the Parque del Oeste, not a mapped front line; no building is destroyed.

landmarks.name: Alcázar of Madrid
landmarks.note: [Certain] fortress built 860-880 by Muhammad I (S3); the Alcazar burned on Christmas Eve 1734 and its remaining walls were demolished in 1738 (S11). [Guessing] a generic walled castle, 80 x 65 m, because the real Alcazar grew irregularly from 1537 and 1636; position = Wikipedia coordinates of the site, no footprint in the data.

landmarks.name: Royal Palace
landmarks.note: [Certain] built 1738-1755 on the site of the Alcazar (S11), square plan around a great square courtyard (S12). [Guessing] 140 x 140 m and 24 m are approximate; POSITION FLAGGED: no footprint within 40 m in buildings.json, so it is a preset at the Wikipedia coordinates, not on real data.

landmarks.name: Museo del Prado
landmarks.note: [Certain] designed in 1785 by Juan de Villanueva, opened in November 1819 (S16). [Guessing] building start taken as the design year 1785; height 17 m, hip roof and colour are approximations; footprint from the cadastre (9,773 m2).

landmarks.name: Almudena Cathedral
landmarks.note: [Certain] first stone 4 April 1883, crypt open in 1911, works practically abandoned until 1950, consecrated 15 June 1993 (S19); main facade faces the Royal Palace (S19). [Guessing] heights and the facade orientation (default axis, not verified in a render); footprint from the cadastre (8,303 m2).

landmarks.name: Teatro Real
landmarks.note: [Certain] groundbreaking 23 April 1818, opened 19 November 1850 (S37). [Guessing] height and roof are approximations; footprint from the cadastre (5,938 m2).

landmarks.name: Cibeles Palace
landmarks.note: [Certain] first stone 1907, opened 14 March 1919 (S20). [Guessing] heights and wing width; footprint from the cadastre (11,768 m2).

landmarks.name: Metropolis Building
landmarks.note: [Certain] designed in 1907 and inaugurated in 1911 (S23). [Guessing] 1911.5 as the opening time within the year; height 30 m and the dome are approximations; footprint from the cadastre (1,273 m2).

landmarks.name: Atocha Station
landmarks.note: [Certain] Madrid's first station opened 9 February 1851; rebuilt after a fire and reopened in 1892; original building taken out of service as a terminal in 1992 (S24). [Guessing] one phase only: the 1892 rebuild and the 1992 conversion are not modelled; start 1850.5 is a modelling choice; footprint from the cadastre (11,840 m2, dated 1992 there).

landmarks.name: Edificio España
landmarks.note: [Certain] construction began 1948, opened in 1953 (S25). [Likely] height 117 m (Wikipedia infobox, not quoted in S25); setbacks default; the cadastre footprint (4,712 m2) sits ~85 m from the Wikipedia point.

landmarks.name: Torre de Madrid
landmarks.note: [Certain] 142 m, 36 floors, built 1954-1957, finished 15 October 1957 (S26). [Guessing] podium and setbacks default; footprint from the cadastre (2,780 m2).

landmarks.name: Cuatro Torres: Torre de Cristal
landmarks.note: [Certain] 249 m, begun 2004, completed 4 December 2008 (S29, S27). Footprint from the cadastre (2,023 m2).

landmarks.name: Cuatro Torres: Torre Emperador
landmarks.note: [Certain] topped out 19 March 2007, 230 m in the Wikipedia infobox (S30); construction began 2004 (S28). [Guessing] Wikipedia's Cuatro Torres page lists a different figure for Torre Espacio (224.5 m); 230 m used. Footprint from the cadastre (1,779 m2).

landmarks.name: Cuatro Torres: Torre Cepsa
landmarks.note: [Certain] second tallest of the four, finished mid-2008 (S28, S32); height 248 m is the Wikipedia infobox value. Footprint from the cadastre (1,869 m2).

landmarks.name: Cuatro Torres: Torre PwC
landmarks.note: [Certain] finished at the end of 2009 (S28), about 236 m (S31). [Guessing] POSITION FLAGGED: the cadastre footprint near the Wikipedia point is only 224 m2, so a 38 x 38 m preset is used and the small cadastre piece stays.

landmarks.name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium
landmarks.note: [Certain] groundbreaking 27 October 1944, construction from June 1945, completed 1947 (S35). [Guessing] 1947.95 as the end of the year; stadium preset with default seating and roof (the 2020s rebuild is not modelled); footprint from the cadastre (44,745 m2, dated 2007 there).

landmarks.name: Puente de Segovia
landmarks.note: [Certain] built 1582-1584 (S47). [Guessing] POSITION FLAGGED: line is centred on the water band of the DEM (about lon -3.7223), +-100 m; width and deck height are approximations.

title: MADRID
860 TO NOW

cards.title: Mayrit rises on the ridge
lines: Emir Muhammad I of Córdoba orders a walled citadel above the Manzanares, sometime between 860 and 880.

cards.title: The Caliphate of Córdoba
lines: Abd al-Rahman III takes the title of caliph in 929; by the late 10th century Mayrit is a frontier stronghold.

cards.title: The caliphate breaks apart
lines: In 1031 it fractures into independent taifa kingdoms; Madrid lies within the Taifa of Toledo at its greatest extent.

cards.title: Madrid passes to Castile
lines: The town goes to Christian rule with the conquest of Toledo; historians debate 1083 or 1085.

cards.title: A suburb beyond the wall
lines: The Arrabal of San Martín, known from 1126, is the first suburb outside the old walls.

cards.title: A wall still unfinished
lines: The Fuero of 1202 still orders the council's fines spent on the wall until it is finished.

cards.title: A wall for the suburbs
lines: Most likely around 1438, a second wall encloses the eastern suburbs; its exact course is uncertain.

cards.title: A royal mint
lines: The town strikes its own coins from 1467 to 1471.

cards.title: A town of 5,000
lines: About 5,000 people live in Madrid around 1480.

cards.title: The Comuneros rise
lines: Rebels depose the royal corregidor by 17 June 1520.

cards.title: The court settles in Madrid
lines: Philip II moves the court; with no official declaration, Madrid becomes the de facto capital.

cards.title: A wall for taxes and health
lines: Philip II's wall of 1566 controls goods and guards against disease.

cards.title: Nearly 100,000 people
lines: From some 20,000 in 1560, the new capital approaches 100,000 by 1590.

cards.title: The court leaves for Valladolid
lines: The capital sits in Valladolid from 1601 to 1606, and Madrid's population reportedly halves.

cards.title: Plaza Mayor is finished
lines: Juan Gómez de Mora's arcaded square is completed in 1619.

cards.title: Philip IV's wall
lines: A brick-and-earth wall of about 13 km encloses 500 hectares, over 150 of them the royal Retiro.

cards.title: Fire in the Plaza Mayor
lines: The first of several fires hits the new square in 1631.

cards.title: The Buen Retiro
lines: The Count-Duke of Olivares commissions a royal park and palace in the 1630s.

cards.title: The Bourbons arrive
lines: Habsburg rule ends in 1700; the succession war brings Philip V to the throne.

cards.title: The Alcázar burns
lines: A Christmas Eve fire destroys the old royal alcázar; it burns for four days.

cards.title: A new palace
lines: Work begins in 1738 on a new Royal Palace, on the alcázar's site.

cards.title: The Royal Palace is done
lines: Finished in 1755: a square plan around a great square courtyard.

cards.title: The Esquilache riots
lines: Street lamps, taxes and a ban on traditional capes set off riots in March 1766.

cards.title: The Puerta de Alcalá
lines: Charles III's monumental gate, inaugurated in 1778, replaces a smaller one in the city wall.

cards.title: A building by Villanueva
lines: Juan de Villanueva designs the building that will become the Prado.

cards.title: The Plaza Mayor burns again
lines: A fire in 1790 destroys nearly a third of the square.

cards.title: The Second of May
lines: On 2 May 1808, Madrileños revolt against the French troops.

cards.title: The French are driven out
lines: On 12 August 1812, English and Portuguese troops enter Madrid after the French defeat at Salamanca.

cards.title: The Prado opens
lines: The royal museum opens to the public in November 1819.

cards.title: Convents are confiscated
lines: Church property is seized in 1835-1836; convents are demolished and streets widened.

cards.title: The Teatro Real opens
lines: Isabella II opens the opera house on 19 November 1850.

cards.title: The first railway station
lines: Madrid's first station opens at Atocha on 9 February 1851.

cards.title: Puerta del Sol takes its modern shape (1862)
lines: Puerta del Sol takes its modern shape (1862)

cards.title: Water from the Lozoya
lines: The Canal de Isabel II is inaugurated on 24 June 1858.

cards.title: The Ensanche plan
lines: A royal decree of 19 July 1860 approves Carlos María de Castro's expansion plan.

cards.title: Puerta del Sol rebuilt
lines: The square takes its modern shape in works from 1857 to 1862.

cards.title: Walls down, Retiro open
lines: After the Glorious Revolution of September 1868, Philip IV's wall is torn down and the Retiro becomes a public park.

cards.title: The first trams
lines: The Salamanca–Sol–Pozas line brings Madrid's first collective transport in 1871.

cards.title: Almudena's first stone
lines: King Alfonso XII lays the first stone of the future cathedral on 4 April 1883.

cards.title: Atocha is rebuilt
lines: After a fire, the railway company rebuilds the station; it reopens in 1892.

cards.title: Over half a million
lines: The census counts 540,109 people in 1900.

cards.title: The Gran Vía begins
lines: King Alfonso XIII opens the works in April 1910, 'an axe blow on the map'.

cards.title: The Metropolis Building
lines: Inaugurated in 1911 on Alcalá Street, after five homes were demolished.

cards.title: Cibeles Palace opens (1919)
lines: Cibeles Palace opens (1919)

cards.title: Cibeles Palace opens
lines: The new post and telegraph palace opens on 14 March 1919.

cards.title: The first Metro line
lines: On 17 October 1919, Alfonso XIII opens the Metro from Sol to Cuatro Caminos, eight stops.

cards.title: The Gran Vía is complete
lines: The last section is finished in 1929.

cards.title: The Second Republic
lines: Proclaimed on 14 April 1931; that year the Casa de Campo opens to the public.

cards.title: The coup fails in Madrid
lines: Workers and loyal troops storm the Cuartel de la Montaña on 20 July 1936.

cards.title: The first air raid
lines: On 27–28 August 1936, Madrid is bombed from the air for the first time.

cards.title: The siege begins
lines: Besieged from October 1936, Madrid sees its fiercest fighting that November.

cards.title: Madrid falls
lines: The city falls to the Nationalists on 28 March 1939.

cards.title: The Bernabéu opens
lines: Real Madrid's stadium is completed in 1947.

cards.title: A much bigger city
lines: Between 1948 and 1954, Madrid annexes 13 surrounding municipalities.

cards.title: Edificio España
lines: The tallest building in Spain opens on the Plaza de España in 1953.

cards.title: The Torre de Madrid
lines: At 142 m and 36 floors, it is finished on 15 October 1957.

cards.title: The M-30 ring road
lines: Building starts in 1970; the first two sections are completed in 1974.

cards.title: The M-30 ring road is built (1970)
lines: Hover area is hand-set on the Manzanares stretch of the M-30.

cards.title: Franco dies
lines: He dies on 20 November 1975; the city's population peaks the same year.

cards.title: A new constitution
lines: Spain approves its democratic constitution by referendum in December 1978.

cards.title: Atocha's new terminal
lines: The old Atocha building leaves service as a terminal in 1992.

cards.title: Almudena is consecrated
lines: Pope John Paul II consecrates the cathedral on 15 June 1993.

cards.title: The Teatro Real reborn
lines: It reopens as an opera house on 11 October 1997.

cards.title: March 11, 2004
lines: Train bombings kill 191 people and injure 1,800.

cards.title: The towers rise
lines: Torre Emperador tops out on 19 March 2007, at 230 m.

cards.title: Spain's tallest tower
lines: Torre de Cristal, 249 m, is completed on 4 December 2008.

cards.title: A hub under Sol
lines: A commuter-rail interchange under the Puerta del Sol opens on 27 June 2009.

cards.title: The M-30 goes underground
lines: Tunnels bury the M-30 along the Manzanares; works end in 2010-2011 and the surface becomes a park.

cards.title: A city of 3.4 million
lines: The municipal register counts 3,416,771 people.
